messages.content: Create at most two reusable medical-image reading skills from this training example. The saved answer/reason may be wrong. Return only JSON {"skills":[{"category":"general or one supplied official category","trigger":"when to apply","steps":["concrete image check","how to distinguish alternatives"]}]}. No case/patient ID, option letter, figure number, patient-specific number, copied question, or rule merely repeating the reference diagnosis. General medical findings are allowed. Based on the chest X-ray images, what is the most accurate description of the changes in the azygos lobe and fissure following the pneumothorax and subsequent reexpansion of the lung in this patient?

A) The azygos fissure is more prominent in Figure 3a compared to Figure 1a, indicating increased pleural separation.
B) The teardrop-shaped opacity is absent in Figure 3a, suggesting a medial displacement of the azygos vein.
C) The azygos lobe has shifted laterally in Figure 3a, as evidenced by a wider separation of the pleural layers.
D) The azygos fissure in Figure 3a shows new pleural adhesions not present in Figure 1a.
E) The teardrop-shaped opacity remains unchanged between Figure 1a and Figure 3a.
F) The azygos fissure is absent in Figure 3a, indicating total resorption of the pneumothorax.
